LSI hasu “cow” is homonymous with linked Badaga hasu “hunger” (DEDR 3825), which is semantically unrelated; cow ancestry remains unresolved.

LSI colle heṇṇu “good woman” has a secure second component (DEDR 4395), but colle differs from the other volle “good” responses and from Kannada oḷḷe (DEDR 1017); hold the whole response rather than silently emend colle.
LSI klia “down” may be a clipped form of kelage (DEDR 1619), but the source spelling lacks the expected medial sequence; no direct comparator was found.
LSI vottura “near” has no secure DEDR family match or checked immediate donor.
LSI dura “far” resembles an Indo-Aryan dūra word, but no verified immediate donor node or borrowing path is established.
LSI u “and” is a grammatical conjunction; the short spelling does not distinguish a native clitic from a borrowed one, and no safe lexical parent is established.
LSI āle “but” is homonymous with linked Badaga āle “house” and another āle “young”, neither semantically relevant; the conjunction needs separate evidence.
LSI haudu “yes” resembles a wider Kannada affirmative, but the exact derivation from a Dravidian verb or demonstrative is not established by the checked DEDR articles.
LSI vokaliga “cultivator” resembles a Kannada social/occupational label; no exact DEDR family or immediate donor node has been verified.
LSI āḍukāra “shepherd” appears built on goat āḍu (DEDR 5152) plus an occupational -kāra element, but the latter and the whole derivation remain unresolved.
LSI dēvaru “God” resembles a Sanskritic deva form; the immediate donor and graph parent are not established, so no remote Sanskrit leap is proposed.
LSI piśāci “Devil” is a learned-looking South Asian term, but the immediate donor attestation and path are not established.
LSI āle “House” matches a Badaga dictionary house term, but DEDR āle articles 382, 384 and 387 mean banyan, hail/water and sugar-cane press; no secure ancestry is established.
LSI klatte “Ass” is near Kannada katte and Toda katy in DEDR 1364, but its extra l is not explained by an attested Badaga comparator or source note.
LSI voṭṭe “Camel” lacks a matching DEDR animal term or established immediate donor.

Third LSI hasu “Cow” record retained separately; linked Badaga hasu “hunger” (DEDR 3825) is a different homonym and not cow evidence.
LSI hakkilu “Bird” matches linked Badaga dictionary bird forms, but those point to unlinked akki variants rather than a validated etymon; immediate ancestry is unresolved.
LSI hūva “Cock” has no secure DEDR bird family match or immediate donor.

LSI sime batu “Duck” is a multiword response, and neither lexical element has a verified etymon or immediate donor in the checked articles.
